strategy.summary: createBookings() books, lists and cancels meeting rooms against a BookingStore (memoryStore in tests). The tests must prove the booking rules (room, owner, UTC half-hour start, 30–240 min length in 30-min steps) with a BookingError naming the reason, the same-room overlap rule including back-to-back and cross-room bookings, listing by start time, and owner-only cancellation that frees the slot.
inScope: BookingError type and its message for each refusal
outOfScope: The app's database-backed BookingStore (not in this repository)
assumptions: Unit tests against the real createBookings() with the real memoryStore(); nothing is faked.
"Says why" is checked by asserting the exact message src/bookings.ts gives each refusal (the module under test is the only source of these messages), plus that the error is a BookingError.
Room names match exactly (case-sensitive), as the code does: 'atlas' is refused.
A start is on the hour/half hour only if it has zero seconds and milliseconds in UTC; a local offset like +05:45 that lands on :15 UTC is refused.

risks.description: Off-by-one in overlap check (<= vs <) would refuse back-to-back bookings or allow touching overlaps
risks.mitigation: TC9 books exactly adjacent slots on both sides; TC7 covers every overlap shape including 30-minute partial overlaps

risks.description: Length/start validation boundaries (30, 240, non-multiples, non-UTC offsets) drift
risks.mitigation: TC4–TC6 table the boundary values on both sides

risks.description: A non-owner can cancel, or cancelling leaves the slot blocked
risks.mitigation: TC11 rebooks the freed slot; TC12 shows the booking survives a stranger's cancel

acceptanceCriteria.text: A booking must name room Atlas, Borealis or Cosmos and a non-blank owner, start on the hour or half hour in UTC, and last 30–240 minutes in 30-minute steps; otherwise book() rejects with a BookingError whose message says why.
A booking overlapping another booking of the same room is rejected with a BookingError; bookings of different rooms never clash and a booking may start exactly when another ends.
list(room) returns that room's bookings ordered by start time.
Only the booking's owner can cancel it (others get a BookingError and the booking stays); cancelling removes it and frees its time for a new booking.

testCases.title: books each of the rooms Atlas, Borealis and Cosmos on the half hour
steps: it.each over ROOMS: book room, owner 'ada', start 09:30Z, 30 minutes
testCases.expected: Returns booking {id 1, room, owner 'ada', start 09:30Z, end 10:00Z}
testCases.rationale: Proves every named room and a half-hour start are accepted

testCases.title: refuses a room that is not Atlas, Borealis or Cosmos
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError, message 'There is no room called "<room>".'

testCases.title: refuses a booking without the name of the person making it
steps: it.each owner '' and '   ': book Atlas 09:00Z 60 min
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'A booking needs the name of the person making it.'

testCases.title: refuses a start that is not on the hour or the half hour in UTC
steps: it.each start 09:15Z, 09:00:30Z, 09:00:00.001Z, 09:00+05:45 (03:15Z), Invalid Date: book Atlas 60 min
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'A booking starts on the hour or the half hour.'
testCases.rationale: Start boundary, including UTC vs local offset

testCases.title: accepts the shortest and longest lengths, 30 minutes and 4 hours
refuses a length outside 30 minutes to 4 hours or not in steps of 30 minutes
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'A booking lasts from 30 minutes to 4 hours, in steps of 30 minutes.'
testCases.rationale: Length boundaries just outside and step rule

testCases.title: refuses a booking that overlaps another booking of the same room
steps: it.each overlap shape: same slot, starts inside (10:30 60m), ends inside (09:30 60m), contains (09:00 180m), contained (10:00 30m): bob books Atlas
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'Atlas is already booked from 2026-03-02T10:00:00.000Z.'; list holds only ada's booking
testCases.rationale: Core double-booking rule, every overlap shape

testCases.title: books different rooms for the same time
testCases.expected: Both succeed; each room lists its one booking

testCases.title: books a room starting exactly when another booking ends
testCases.expected: Both succeed; Atlas lists three bookings

testCases.title: lists a room's bookings by start time
steps: Book Atlas 14:00, 09:00, 11:30 (in that order) and Borealis 10:00
testCases.expected: Exactly the three Atlas bookings ordered 09:00, 11:30, 14:00 (ids 2, 3, 1)
testCases.rationale: Ordering independent of insertion order, scoped to room

testCases.title: lets the person who made a booking cancel it and frees its time
testCases.expected: Cancel resolves; list holds only the 12:00 booking; bob's booking succeeds
testCases.rationale: Owner cancel and freeing the slot

testCases.title: refuses to cancel a booking for someone who did not make it
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'Only the person who made a booking can cancel it.'; booking still listed

testCases.title: refuses to cancel a booking that does not exist
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'There is no booking 99.'; ada's booking still listed

review.standard: Reuse the repo's helpers … A helper two specs need goes once in a helper module
review.summary: The `at()` time helper repeats the one in test/bookings.test.ts:5, with a different input format (`at('09:00')` there appends `:00Z`, here only `Z`), so the two spec files now have same-named helpers that take different strings.
review.failureScenario: Someone copies a call such as `at('09:00:30')` from this file into test/bookings.test.ts, gets `2026-03-02T09:00:30:00Z`, which is an Invalid Date, and the test then checks a different refusal than intended. Moving one `at` into a shared helper module (e.g. test/support/time.ts) that both specs import would fix this.

review.standard: Arrange / Act / Assert … with a title that states it
review.summary: The overlap table's title template `refuses one that $shape` produces ungrammatical test names for two rows ('refuses one that the same slot', 'refuses one that contains it' reads fine but 'the same slot' does not).
review.failureScenario: When the same-slot row fails, the report shows 'refuses one that the same slot', which is harder to read than a name that states the behaviour. Rewording the shape to 'is the same slot' fixes it.
